We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically to the given molecule (target) reproduces an SN2 reaction: C-N formed and C-Cl broken, breaking a halide functional group. So we need a template that corresponds to SN2 substitution of a halide (Cl) by a nucleophile (e.g., amine). The target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

Let's examine: It has a methoxy phenyl, attached to an amide linking to a triazine? Actually c2nnn(...). There's a side chain Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. That side chain includes a benzylic carbon attached to N4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine?). No halide present? The target may have a chlorine originally that got substituted by something. But the target SMILES doesn't show Cl. So the retrosynthetic step would break a C-N bond (new C-N formed) and form a C-Cl bond (leaving group). So we need to find a template that breaks a C-N bond and forms a C-Cl bond (i.e., reverse of SN2). The forward reaction: C-Cl + N nucleophile -> C-N + Cl-.

Thus retrosynthetic: target (C-N) -> precursor: C-Cl (leaving group) + nucleophile (maybe amine). So we need a template where functional_groups_broken includes "halide" (since forward breaks halide) and functional_groups_formed includes "amine"? Actually forward forms C-N bond, so functional_groups_formed includes "amine"? The description says "C-N formed and C-Cl gone breaking an 'halide' functional group". So forward: halide broken, amine formed. So in retrosynthesis search, we set functional_groups_broken = ["halide"]? Wait broken in forward = halide broken. So we set functional_groups_broken = ["halide"]; functional_groups_formed = ["amine"] maybe "primary amine" or "secondary amine". The nucleophile could be amine. So we search templates.

Let's call search_template_catalog_by_criteria with molecule_smiles = target, functional_groups_broken = "halide", functional_groups_formed = "primary amines" or "secondary amines". The list includes "primary amines", "secondary amines", "tertiary amines". The target has a secondary amine (the N attached to aromatic). So maybe "secondary amines". Let's try both.
